plan.english: Now hear what the king set down. Whoever steals cattle, then let him pay ten rams. If a thief drives two horses away, then let him pay four horses. If he hides the cattle and the watcher sees him, then let the watcher seize him. Whoever kills the thief in the house, let him not pay. Whoever buys a ram from a thief, then let him pay twice.

Whoever has swift horses, let him guard them. If a man steals a horse from a brother, then let him give the brother two horses. Whoever kills a brother's horse, then let him bring three rams. If a man finds a thief in a hedge, then let him seize him. Whoever steals the queen's horse, then let him die. May the swift horses live!

Whoever cuts off the beard of a father-in-law, then let him give five gifts. Whoever hits the mouth of a husband's brother, then let him give three rams. Whoever splits the jaw of a brother-in-law, then let him leave the village. Whoever breaks a brother's shoulder, then let him bring wine. Whoever strikes the queen, let him not live.

Let the master of the house carry water to the guest. Then let him seat the guest inside. Let the guest eat the grain and drink the wine. Whoever drives him out of the house, then let him pay three rams. Whoever kills a guest at the fire, let him not live. When the guest goes out, then let the master give him a gift.

Let the boundary be a hedge. Whoever moves the boundary, then let him leave the village. Whoever cuts off the hedge, then let him give a gift. Whoever comes into a brother's field, let him not eat the barley. Let a hill be the border. Let a hedge stand between two fields. Let the man with a hundred cows point out the border. May the boundary stand.

When a father dies, the sons shall take the house, and they shall take the horses. If he has no son, the daughter shall take the field. If he has no daughter, his brother shall take the field. Let the brothers not drive the sister out of the house. May the daughter be glad. Let the daughter not go out.

Whoever leads a wife into the house, then let him give the bride-price to the father-in-law. If the wife leaves him, then let the father-in-law give the bride-price again. If the husband dies, then let the husband's brother protect the daughter-in-law. Let the daughter-in-law sit down by the fire. If the brother-in-law comes in, then let the daughter-in-law give him water. Let the son-in-law not strike the father-in-law.

Whoever gives a pledge, let him guard it. Whoever breaks the pledge, may Father Sky strike him down. Let Mother Earth hear the word. Let the sun look at the pledge. If two brothers speak, then let them give a pledge. Whoever hears the pledge, let him remember it. Let the pledge be a cord.

Whoever guards sheep, if a wolf devours a ram, let him not bring a ram. Whoever milks the sheep of a daughter-in-law, then let him pay two rams. Whoever cuts off the wool of the ram, then let him give three gifts. Let the ram go with the sheep. Whoever sees a snake, let him speak a word.

Whoever burns a house, then let him build it again. Whoever's fire burns the field of a father-in-law, he shall give two gifts to the father-in-law. Whoever carries fire into a house, then let him leave the village. If the village burns, come, men, and carry water! Let it be near the fire.

Whoever has a dog, let him feed it. If a dog kills a man, then let the master of the dog bring wine to the kin. If a dog kills a wolf, may it be glad. If a man hits a dog, then let him give a ram to its master. Let the dog guard the ram, and let the wolf not seize it. Let the dog not step into the house of a brother-in-law. May the dog lie down.

title: The Law of Gifts to the Rulers

plan.english: Let him who has a hundred cows bring the king ten cattle. Whoever has sheep, let him give the queen wool. Whoever has a swift horse, let him lead it to the queen's daughter. Whoever hides a gift, then let him pay twice. Whoever has no cattle, then let him give a gift. May the king be a giver of good things.

title: The Law of the Ploughed Field

plan.english: Whoever ploughs, then let him eat the grain. Whoever ploughs the field of a father-in-law, then he shall not take the grain. Whoever ploughs with the cattle of a husband's brother, then let him give barley to the husband's brother. Whoever breaks the quern of a daughter-in-law, then let him give a quern. May the barley increase. May the ears of grain grow.

Whoever buys a horse, then let him look at the mouth of the horse. Let him carry the price. Whoever buys wine, then let him give a gift. If two brothers buy a house, then let them pay ten rams. Whoever does not give the price, he shall not seize it. May there be selling in the village. Let the watcher speak the word.

Whoever kills a man, then let the kin of the dead man take ten gifts. If the kin do not take them, then let the striker die. Whoever kills one of the kin, let him not sit at the fire. If a brother kills a brother, then let the watcher lead the striker out of the house. May the dead man lie in the earth. May his name be famous.

Whoever has seen the thief, then let him speak the word. Let the watcher say what he saw. Whoever knows the boundary, then let him show it. Let the man with a hundred cows listen to the words. Let the young man remember them. Whoever is afraid, let him not tremble.

The guest arrived at the house. Then the master spoke: "Who are you?" "Where are you going?" Then he said: "I am going to my brother. Now I became tired. Let me sit by your fire." Then the master said: "Sit down inside. Drink water. Guest, do not be afraid. May Dawn give you good things."

Then the master said: "Whose son are you?" Then he spoke: "My father has a hundred cows. My brother dwells in the village." "I know your father. I saw him yesterday." "Is he alive?" "He lives. His name is famous." "Now I became glad."

Then the guest said: "Dawn became bright. Now I am going." Then the master said: "Take the gift." "Your gift is great. I shall remember your house." "May your horses be swift. May Mother Earth protect you." Then he said: "Brother, may you live."

Then the king said: "What did you see, watcher?" Then he said: "I saw three men driving four horses." "Whose are the horses?" "I do not know it. The horses are swift." "Go, watcher, and lead the men to me." "Now I shall go." "May the gods protect us."

title: The King and the Old Man

plan.english: Then the king said: "What do you remember, old man?" Then he said: "I remember your father. He was a great man. He slew the serpent. Imperishable fame followed him. He died; now his name is famous." Then he said: "May my name be famous. May good fame follow me." Then the old man said: "Men die. Fame does not vanish."

Then the father-in-law said: "Son-in-law, hear my words. Do not strike your brother-in-law. Carry water and wine to the daughter-in-law. Bring a ram to the gods. Do not steal wool." Then he said: "I am listening, father-in-law. I shall remember them." Then the father-in-law said: "Guard the house, son-in-law. Son-in-law, may you live."

Then the old brother said: "Mother is dead. Let us split the cattle in two." Then the young one said: "Which of the two horses will you take?" "I shall take the swift horse." "I shall take the field." "Let the house be yours." Then he said: "You are good, brother. May we be brothers."

Then the brother said: "You stole my ram!" Then he said: "I did not steal your ram." "Who saw the thief?" "I saw the wolf on the hill. It seized the ram." "Give me a pledge." Then he said: "May Father Sky strike me down, if I stole it." Then he said: "Brother, I am confident. Let us drink wine."

Then the daughter-in-law said: "Husband's brother, the cattle became tired. Now I am thirsty." Then he said: "Drink water, daughter-in-law. The sun is high. Let us lead them to the hedge. Let us sit and eat the grain." "May the grain grow." "May the ears of grain fill."

Then the daughter said: "Who put the sun in the sky?" Then he said: "The gods put it." "What drinks water and does not become full?" "The earth drinks it, and it does not become full." "What lies on the hill and does not move?" "The boundary lies on the hill and does not move." "What is red?" "Fire is red." "You know, father."

Then the father said: "Daughter, a man came to the house. He is seeking you." Then the daughter said: "Who is he?" "He is one who has a hundred cows. Ten gifts are the bride-price." "I do not know him. Is he good?" Then he said: "He is young." "Let me look at him." "May the gods lead a good husband to you."

Then the father-in-law said: "Daughter-in-law, bring the wool. Dress yourself with it; it is winter." Then she said: "Father-in-law, where are the sheep?" "They are on the hill. The ram stands by the hedge." "Father-in-law, I am afraid." "The wolf is near." "Daughter-in-law, do not tremble. I shall guard them." "I am going to them."

title: Sister and Brother at the Water

plan.english: Then the sister said: "Brother, I am thirsty. Give me water." Then he said: "Drink, sister. It became cold." "Do not push me!" "I am not pushing you. Look at the duck! It is swimming." "I see the duck. Now let us swim." "Sister, I am afraid."

Then the son-in-law said: "Father-in-law, I give you ten gifts and two horses. This is the bride-price." Then the father-in-law said: "The bride-price is great. Son-in-law, sit down and eat the grain." "Where is my wife?" "The wife is in the house with the mother." "I shall protect my wife." "May you be a good son-in-law."

Then the wife said: "Husband, where were you?" Then he said: "I was working on the hill. I became tired." "Come to the house. Eat the grain. I cooked it." "Where is the daughter?" "She is sitting inside." "Wife, give me wine." "Drink the wine and speak now."

Then the queen said: "King, two men came to the house. They are seeking our daughter." Then he said: "Who are they?" "The old man has a hundred cows. The young man has nimble horses." "Let our daughter look at them." "Then let her speak." Then the queen said: "May Dawn, the daughter of Sky, lead a husband to her."

The Brown One drove the rams to the hill. The Nimble One is the son of the Brown One. The Nimble One led the sheep, and he milked them. The Alone One is born from the Nimble One. The Alone One built a house. Then he killed the wolf. Great fame followed him. He died; now his name is famous. The Whole One is the daughter of the Alone One. She wore wool. Now they are famous.

The old king slew the serpent. Great fame followed him. His son is a giver of good things. The giver gave gifts to the gods and to the kin. The Free One is born from the giver. The Free One drove four swift horses. The Free One took a wife. Their daughter is the mother of the Heavy One. The Heavy One became king. The Heavy One set a name for the daughter. The Heavy One died; his fame is imperishable.

The Wide One had two horses. The two horses were swift. The Wide One nourished them. The High One is the son of the Wide One. The High One joined them to the wheel. The Sharp One is born from the High One. The Sharp One drove a horse. He carried the barley. Great fame has reached him. He lay down. The name of the horses is famous.

The old man spoke words. The gods heard them. The Trembling One is born from him. The Trembling One spoke words to the gods. The gods became glad. The Pure One is born from the Trembling One. His mouth was sharp. The Pure One gave a ram to the sun. The Pure One sat on the hill. The Pure One went away.

The Old One milked the sheep. A daughter is born from her. The daughter lifted the wool. The daughter dressed herself. The daughter is the mother of the Double One. The Double One cooked the grain. The Double One is the daughter-in-law of the father-in-law. She protected the house. The Held One is the daughter of the Double One. The Held One nourished the ram. The Held One lay down; Mother Earth covered her.

The Heavy One ploughed the field with four cattle. He placed the boundary. The Wet One is the son of the Heavy One. The Wet One built a hedge. The Mixed One is born from the Wet One. The Mixed One bought a house with ten rams. Barley grew. The Mixed One lifted the quern. Then he lay down. Mother Earth covered him.

The queen has twins. The two brothers grew up. They dwelt in the village. A wolf seized the duck. They saw it. They slew it. The queen gave a gift to the brothers. The young one vanished. The Alone One lived. He worked. His fame is imperishable.

A wolf seized the sheep. The Strong One slew it. He rescued the sheep. The Burning One is the son of the Strong One. The Burning One seized the thief. The thief became afraid. The Burning One led him to the village. The Blue One is born from the Burning One. The Blue One slew the serpent. The name of the Blue One is famous.
